entries.proposition: Convergent mixed-methods survey of 267 parents of children with severe developmental impairments.
entries.snippet: A total of 267 parents completed the questionnaire.

entries.proposition: Recruitment through advocacy groups of several DEE conditions via an online survey in 2023.
entries.snippet: Parental advocacy groups representing several DEEs within the DEE‐P Connections network (https://deepconnections.net/) invited their members to participate in a survey administered online in CLIRINX 14 between June and November 2023.
Severely impaired communication was an essential eligibility criterion.

entries.proposition: Parents wrote the smallest improvement that would be important to them: a hypothetical wish, not a measured change.
entries.snippet: For each top domain, they described in open text the smallest improvement or step forward in that area that would be important to them or their child (i.e. a ‘wish’) and explained why that improvement would be important.

entries.proposition: Expressive communication was the priority for 79 percent, gross motor 39 percent and receptive communication 27 percent.
entries.snippet: expressive communication was the most frequently identified priority (79.4%) followed by gross motor skills (38.6%) and receptive communication (27.3%).

entries.proposition: Most of the children had severe or profound communication impairment; 78 percent seldom or never communicated effectively even with familiar people.
entries.snippet: Seldom or never communicates effectively even with familiar people | 199 (78%)

entries.proposition: Meaning and purpose codes (preferences, pain) occurred at all communication levels; non-verbal modes were more frequent with greater impairment.
entries.snippet: Codes for meaning and purpose (e.g. demonstrating preference, expressing emotions) were represented across all levels of communication impairment

entries.proposition: For children unable to walk, meaningful gross-motor codes concerned head control, leg strength for transfers and sitting.
entries.snippet: For example, codes for those unable to walk included gaining head control or leg strength to assist transfers, whereas codes for individuals with less impairment referred to independent walking.

entries.proposition: Supplement: among 85 wishes for children unable to walk, the most frequent code was sitting independently (20), then head control and assisting transfers.
entries.snippet: Walks with assistance / n=8 wishes | Unable to walk / n=85 wishes

entries.proposition: Supplement: for children seldom or never communicating, the most frequent code was basic communication of needs, wants and likes (49).
entries.snippet: 1 | Express feelings/emotions (n=2) | Basic communication of needs/wants/likes (n=6) | Basic communication of needs/wants/likes (n=49)

entries.proposition: The FDA is said to prefer individual worthwhile change over average-group minimal important differences.
entries.snippet: preferred by the US Food and Drug Administration over minimal clinical important difference values which are average group changes.

entries.proposition: Measurement implication: functional instruments should be paired with broader instruments such as quality of life.
entries.snippet: COAs of functioning should be accompanied by broader COAs, such as quality of life, to indicate whether the meaningful change has achieved wider impact in how the child lives.

entries.proposition: Limits: convenience sample, unable to probe responses, some responses non-specific, little epilepsy phenotype data.
entries.snippet: However, this was a convenience sample which might not be representative of the population. We were unable to probe the expressed concepts.

entries.proposition: Fig 1 graphical abstract: 267 parents of children aged 12 months or older, mixed methods, directed content analysis giving 86 codes; common codes include communicating preferences, sitting, walking, grasping, eating.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Graphical abstract: Participants (n=267, parents of children at least 12 months, severe communication impairments, 88.4 percent genetic cause); Mixed methods (quantitative: communication, gross and fine motor, eating levels; qualitative: smallest meaningful improvement and why); Directed content analysis giving 86 codes; common, some spanning impairment levels and some specific codes; interpretation: codes indicate components for clinical-trial evaluations.
